dimensions.instrument_fault_found_and_fixed: _jl1look.mjs defaulted BEFORE to an absolute path into the SHARED checkout. Once the judge applied the round there, "before" and "after" became the same file: the sheet showed the new legends in the BEFORE row and the control passed BY CONSTRUCTION, because a file is byte-identical to itself. The judge looked at that sheet and nearly accepted it. This is §6.1 in a new place — a CONTROL that is a function of whatever the tree happens to hold at run time — and it is worse than a wrong number because it produces a picture, and D12 is the one check that is supposed not to run on a prior. BEFORE is now required, with no default, and the run throws if the two revisions are byte-identical.

why_wrong: The first sentence is true and the second does not follow. _x6dark.mjs is indeed reverse-only, but every coin's OWN round-0 instrument measured D13-obverse and every one of those values is in this coin's scorecard. The judge generalised from one instrument's scope to the whole rubric without opening the scorecards it had already written — the same class of error as reading a description instead of the artefact (Q5), with the judge's own prior standing in for the description.
set_finding: Read across the four coins the obverse D13 failures share a sign and a cause: at the icon tier our busts are TOO DARK against their fields (delta -0.0788 to -0.2537) and carry roughly TWICE the reference ink (cent 0.74 vs 0.337, nickel 0.644 vs 0.402, quarter 0.802 vs 0.634). That is the opposite sign to the dime REVERSE, which is too light and too sparse. One is a set-wide property of how the bust mass and its relief survive downscaling; the other is one drawing. They are different repairs and should not be dispatched together.

the_finding: The references are not the problem and neither, mainly, is the rule. The four references agree on the DESIGN trivially — it is the same design — and their thresholded masks agree only at IoU ~0.36-0.53. What varies between them is lighting, finish and specular behaviour on struck metal, and a threshold mask records that variation as shape. The quarter hit the same wall in its round 0 (three thresholds agreeing at IoU 0.47-0.69). That is now TWO coins, and it is evidence about the RUBRIC rather than about either coin: D2's 0.95/0.97 gates may not be reachable by thresholding any photograph of a struck coin. Per 8 the honest verdict is ESCALATE, never a lowered gate.
the_constructive_path: COIN-JUDGE 2.1 already says it: "a hand annotation is a legitimate frozen target", and R3 says try the overlay before you block. That path was NOT available before today — it needs a reference good enough to trace. dime-pcgs2015-pair.jpg at ~870px across is good enough. So the acquisition DID unblock D2; it unblocked it for hand annotation rather than for automatic segmentation. Tracing a motif outline is a judgment task and routes to the owner or to a judge session dedicated to it, not to a specialist.
